messages.subject: mapdata china and ggplot
parts:
Hello
I am new and impressed but a bit lost.
I want to use the hires map of china including provinces in ggplot.
 
If I plot using map it looks good.
 
library("ggplot2")
requirePackage(mapdata) ; requirePackage(maps);requirePackage(mapproj);

 map('china') #just a map
 
 
But in ggplot:
 
china_reg <- map_data("china")
p <- ggplot()
p <- p + geom_polygon( data=china_reg, aes(x=long, y=lat, group = region),
colour="black", fill="yellow", alpha=0.3 )
p
 
looks strange and angled, and double lines etc.
 
I have ordered the manual book etc and searched the web but ... -  I am sure someone can give me a quick answer here.
I will listen and learn.
Thanks!
O

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: mapdata china and ggplot
parts:
Hi,

I think the data is just not so good. You get the same problem with

map("china", fill=TRUE)

You can get the equivalent of map("china") in ggplot2 with

china_reg2 <- fortify(map("china", fill=FALSE, plot=FALSE))
p2 <- ggplot(china_reg2)
p2 + geom_path(aes(x=long, y=lat, group = group))

but just as with map(), you won't be able to properly fill the areas.

HTH,
Ista
